events.description: USS The Sullivans refuels in Aden, Yemen.
Attempted attack on a US ship (possibly USS The Sullivans) failed when the overloaded boat stuck in sand at the launch site; timed for the 27th of Ramadan.
Al-Quso delivered $7,000 to Khallad in Bangkok, staying ~10 days before returning to Aden.
Khaled al-Mohdhar arrived in Kuala Lumpur.
CIA internal email discussing timeline and possible identity of 'Khalid' as Khallad.
Attempted attack on a US ship (possibly USS The Sullivans) failed because the boat's weight stuck it in sand at the launch site; timed for the 27th day of Ramadan; perpetrators abandoned the boat.
Al-Nashiri returned to Site 5 to remove the boat with hired truck and crane, then fled to Afghanistan.
Al-Quso, instructed by Ibrahim, traveled from Yemen to Thailand to deliver $7,000 to Khallad in Bangkok, stayed 10 days, returned to Aden.
Possible Bin Ladin associate Khaled al-Mohdhar arrived in Kuala Lumpur.

key_claims: CIA analysts in 2001 considered that the 'Khalid' traveler tracked in early 2000 might actually be Khallad, who was linked to the USS Cole bombing.
Al-Quso travelled to Bangkok in January 2000 to deliver $7,000 to Khallad, apparently money arranged via Ibrahim in Sana'a.
A failed January 2000 boat attack on a US ship in Aden preceded the Cole bombing; al-Nashiri fled to Afghanistan afterward.
Khaled al-Mohdhar, a possible Bin Ladin associate, arrived in Kuala Lumpur in January 2000.
